issues.text: q2, explanation of option a (en and vi): "Git does nothing on a timer; no Git command runs unless you run it" is false for Git 2.54 - git-maintenance start "updates the background scheduler to run git maintenance run --scheduled on an hourly basis", and its prefetch task runs git fetch. What stays true: prefetch writes to refs/prefetch/ so remote-tracking names "stay unmoved unless they initiate a fetch". The key (b) is correct; only the reasoning overreaches.
issues.quote: Git does nothing on a timer; no Git command runs unless you run it.
issues.fix: en: "Nothing in Git moves the `origin/*` names on a timer; they move only when a command you run talks to the server, so the gap is measured from that command, not in minutes." vi: "Không có gì trong Git dịch các tên `origin/*` theo chu kỳ; chúng chỉ dịch khi một lệnh bạn chạy nói chuyện với server, nên khoảng cách tính từ lệnh đó chứ không tính bằng phút."

issues.text: The prerequisite taught me that a commit can name two parents. Two arrows here are labelled "parents" (plural), so my first reading was that 59f8ec8 and 57a2d53 each have two parents. The prose does say these arrows skip commits, but only after I had already misread the diagram.
issues.quote: the two labelled `parents` skip the commits in between, which the output block below prints
issues.fix: Relabel those two arrows in the diagram, e.g. "back through 2 commits" / "back through 3 commits", so they cannot be read as a commit with two parents.

issues.text: "Two of those lines can belong to two people" made me picture two people standing on different names in one repository, one folder. Later I learn each person has their own repository and a server in between. The step connecting the two ideas is missing at this point.
issues.quote: Two of those lines can belong to two people — each stands on a different name, and neither one's commits move the other's.
issues.fix: Add a few words saying each person works in their own copy of the repository (the remote part below explains how the copies meet), or move this sentence to after the `origin` paragraph.

issues.text: Two lines of the first block are never mentioned in the prose: `>/dev/null` after `git branch --set-upstream-to`, and `$(git rev-list --count main)` in the last echo. I can guess the second one counts commits, but I do not know what `>/dev/null` does. Also, `$repo` and `$origin` only get explained at the end of the paragraph, after I had already stopped at them.
issues.fix: Add one clause saying the last line only prints how many commits `main` has and `>/dev/null` hides a confirmation message; move "`$repo` and `$origin` hold the two folder paths" to the start of that paragraph.

issues.text: I read the `origin/HEAD` sentence three times. "A fresh copy of that second repository" introduces a third repository I have not seen, and it does not say whether this matters for anything in the lesson.
issues.quote: `origin/HEAD` names the branch a fresh copy of that second repository is put on first; `git fetch` records it.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "`origin/HEAD` says which branch someone who copies the server repository would start on; you can ignore it in this lesson."

issues.text: The third misconception says the second step of `git pull` "can stop part-way", but it never says why it would stop. "Git halts and asks you to finish that step" restates the claim instead of explaining it, so I cannot picture when this happens.
issues.quote: that second step changes your own history and can stop part-way. Stopping part-way means Git halts and asks you to finish that step.
issues.fix: Add one clause with the cause, e.g. "for example when your branch and the fetched commits changed the same lines", and point to the next lesson for the details.

issues.text: Only **branch** is bolded. HEAD, remote, remote-tracking name and upstream are also defined, but in plain text. I could follow them, but I could not tell which of these five are the words the lesson expects me to keep.
issues.quote: - HEAD — the record of which branch you are standing on
issues.fix: Either bold all five defined terms consistently, or add a note that only "branch" is the term to keep and the other four are working words for this lesson.

issues.text: q3: each option restates almost word for word the sentence that explains that line in section 5 (e.g. "records its path under the name `origin`"), so I can order them by matching the text, not by understanding it. Options a and c also say "the bare repository", a phrase the lesson never uses. It only says `git clone --bare`.
issues.quote: `git remote add origin` records the path of the bare repository under the short name `origin`.
issues.fix: Paraphrase each option by its effect (e.g. "give the second repository a short name") and write "the second repository" instead of "the bare repository".

issues.text: Section 5 contains two scripts, a long output listing and five paragraphs explaining that output. By the time I reached the `ls -1` paragraph ("the point of the lesson"), I had lost track of which block I was reading about.
issues.quote: The two `ls -1` listings are the point of the lesson.
issues.fix: Put a short lead sentence before the second block saying which three things to look at (the `*`, the brackets, the two `ls -1` listings), in that order.
